comparable.analogs: ANALOG 1 — Moderna/Merck mRNA-4157 (V940), KEYNOTE-942 readout (Dec 13, 2022): the archetypal precedent for ELTX's exact pattern — randomized Phase 2 of a personalized neoantigen vaccine + checkpoint in the RESECTED/adjuvant high-risk setting with a survival primary endpoint (RFS), reading out HR 0.56 / 44% risk-of-recurrence-or-death reduction. Shared pre-breakout features vs ELTX/AMPLIFY-7P: adjuvant post-resection population, neoantigen-vaccine MOA, single binary HR-driven DFS/RFS analysis, FDA design engagement. Move: +26% two-day ($165.13->$208.95) plus FDA Breakthrough Therapy; seeded a multi-year mRNA-cancer-vaccine narrative. NOTE: large-cap, so share multiple was modest (~1.3x on the print) — it validates the readout SHAPE/'tell' ELTX is hunting, not the magnitude. ANALOG 2 — small-cap single-randomized-readout re-rate archetype (Madrigal-style, +200%+ on one positive trial print): at ~$209M cap / ~18.4M shares ELTX is a thin event-driven micro-cap where a clean DFS HR plus a partnership/Phase-3 path is the catalyst class that historically re-rates small-caps ~3-10x in one move; peak multiple ~3-10x, time-to-peak days-to-a-few-months around the catalyst.
comparable.failure_case: Gritstone bio (GRTS) — near-identical look-alike: KRAS-directed neoantigen-vaccine company that, at the SAME stage, produced genuinely encouraging randomized Phase 2 data (GRANITE: 27% relative risk reduction of progression/death all-comers, 50% in the low-ctDNA subgroup) yet filed Chapter 11 on Oct 10, 2024 and was delisted (assets sold for $21.25M); round-tripped from ~$18 (Jun-2021) toward zero. What differed from the winners: the drug arguably worked but the company died of CASH exhaustion (~$61.7M, no way to raise) with NO firm Tier-1 partner or non-dilutive bridge to registration — i.e., a positive-ish signal could not save a going-concern shell. This is precisely the ELTX bear case (negative/ambiguous readout -> cash-empty shell diluting toward zero; going-concern already live).
comparable.differentiator: The single feature separating the winner path (Moderna/4157) from the round-tripper (Gritstone) is a FIRM capital/partner bridge to registration, not the efficacy print itself. mRNA-4157 had Merck as a fixed, deep-pocketed development partner funding the Phase 3 (V940-001/KEYNOTE-V940) the instant Phase 2 hit; Gritstone had encouraging data but no partner and ran out of money. For ELTX the discriminating signal to watch is therefore NOT just the DFS HR — it is whether a positive readout converts into a FIRM partnership/non-dilutive financing that funds the agreed Phase 3 before the cash shell forces dilution. Absent that, even a positive DFS can still round-trip (Gritstone proves a 'working' KRAS vaccine is not enough).

The asymmetry is real (binary), but the lead bear is that the de-risking events to date (IDMC "continue without modifications," 99% T-cell response) are SOFT immunogenicity/safety signals, NOT the hard randomized DFS efficacy that the failure graveyard says is the actual hurdle.

Market cap troughed to ~$889M in 2015 (cap-equivalent to QTRX's ~$165M after share-count scaling — both are 'approved/reimbursed but ramp-unproven' small caps). Shared pattern features (not generic): (1) existing screening platform + a discrete regulatory milestone HIT, (2) CMS rate already secured before volume, (3) re-rate hinging entirely on test-volume conversion. Peak ~$155/sh Feb-2021 (~$13-25B cap) = roughly 15-25x; time-to-peak ~6 years, with the decisive inflection in 2017 (volume +136-150% YoY, coverage reaching 86% of target population). SECONDARY (size-matched) — Veracyte (VCYT) ~2015-16: ~$200M cap molecular-Dx franchise on a tools-plus-test base, indeterminate-screening population, reimbursement-led volume ramp — shares QTRX's small-cap Dx-optionality-on-tools profile; ran ~$4-8 to an $86 peak (Feb-2021) ≈ ~15-20x over ~5 years.
comparable.failure_case: GRAIL / Galleri — the round-tripper at the SAME pre-breakout stage. Structurally near-identical to QTRX's setup: a multi-analyte ALGORITHMIC blood test (multi-cancer early detection vs QTRX's multi-analyte AD panel) sold into a mass-screening population, with the entire re-rate thesis resting on adoption + reimbursement optionality. It did NOT multibag — shares fell ~50% (Feb-2026) on a disappointing clinical-utility readout, with only ~$30M/quarter revenue against ~$197M/quarter losses. What differed from the QTRX archetype (and from EXAS): Galleri was marketed WITHOUT FDA approval, had NO secured Medicare/CMS reimbursement, and — decisively — lacked firm clinical-utility data to convert the optionality into covered, physician-ordered volume. The failure traces to the absence of the binary de-riskers (clearance + reimbursement + utility proof), not to valuation or theme. QTRX has already secured the CMS $897 rate and filed its 510(k) (Breakthrough Device), but its FY26 guide still books ZERO testing revenue — so it sits between the EXAS template (milestones converting) and the GRAIL trap (optionality that never converts to FIRM, reimbursed demand).
comparable.differentiator: The single feature that separated the EXAS/VCYT winners from the GRAIL round-tripper — and that QTRX must demonstrate — is CONVERSION of a secured-reimbursement, cleared test into accelerating, payer-covered, physician-ordered VOLUME (firm demand), not announced TAM. EXAS had CMS + FDA AND then proved 150%+ YoY volume growth with coverage to 86% of target; GRAIL had TAM and marketing but no FDA clearance, no CMS coverage, and a clinical-utility readout that failed to convert. QTRX today holds two of the three de-riskers (CMS $897 rate granted; 510(k) filed under Breakthrough Device) but the third — the H2-2026 FDA decision PLUS the three clinical-utility readouts converting into reimbursed test volume — is entirely unproven (FY26 guide = zero testing revenue).
